title: The Camera Inside the Editor: Reading the Implicit Camera of Image Editors with Painted Calibration Patterns
abstract: arXiv:2609.37732v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Instruction-based image editors insert objects, restyle scenes and render new viewpoints, but it is unknown which camera they assume when they paint into a photograph. Asked to cover the floor with a checkerboard, an editor paints projective structure from which classical vanishing-point geometry reads pitch, roll, focal length, yaw and, on renders, the principal point, without any training. Unlike a calibrator such as GeoCalib, which estimates the camera of an image, this isolates the camera under which the editor paints. On 120 rendered cameras with exact ground truth, Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 paints tile edges that meet their vanishing points within 0.26 degrees, and its implicit camera matches the true one to 0.8 degrees in pitch and 6% in focal length, more accurately than GeoCalib except in roll. Asked to draw the horizon or mark a vanishing point instead, the editor fails, so this knowledge is revealed by painting and not by the exp

translated_title: 编辑器内部的相机：通过绘制标定图案读取图像编辑器的隐式相机
translated_abstract: 基于指令的图像编辑器可以插入物体、重新设计场景风格并渲染新的视角，但当它们在照片上作画时，究竟假设了什么样的相机却不得而知。当被要求用棋盘格覆盖地面时，编辑器会绘制出投影结构，经典的灭点几何可以从这些结构中读出俯仰角、横滚角、焦距和偏航角，在渲染图像上还能读出主点，且无需任何训练。与GeoCalib这类估计图像相机的标定工具不同，该方法分离出了编辑器作画时所依据的相机。在120个具有精确真值的渲染相机上，Qwen-Image-Edit-2511绘制的瓷砖边缘与其灭点的交汇偏差在0.26度以内，其隐式相机与真实相机相比俯仰角误差为0.8度、焦距误差为6%，除横滚角外比GeoCalib更准确。然而，当要求编辑器直接绘制地平线或标记灭点时，编辑器却失败了，说明这种知识是通过作画而非直接绘制来显现的。
tldr: 通过让图像编辑器绘制棋盘格等标定图案，可利用经典灭点几何在无需训练的情况下读出编辑器作画时的隐式相机参数（如俯仰角误差0.8度、焦距误差6%），其精度在多数指标上超过GeoCalib，但这种相机知识只能通过作画间接显现，无法直接要求编辑器画出地平线或灭点。
en_tdlr: By prompting instruction-based image editors to paint calibration patterns like checkerboards, classical vanishing-point geometry can extract their implicit camera without any training—achieving 0.8° pitch error and 6% focal length error, outperforming GeoCalib on most metrics—yet this knowledge is only revealed through painting, as the editor fails when asked to directly draw horizons or vanishing points.
